claims.text: The word "II" does not appear anywhere on the cover or title page of this released PDF; the title page reads "(U) Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion". The Roman numeral exists only in The Black Vault's filename. This is why the board carries two nodes with identical labels.

Admin note states the product was produced in FY 2010, whereas the Acquisition Threat Support DIRDs in this batch state FY 2009. The DIRD series therefore spans at least two fiscal years and two internal DIA series labels.

This is NOT a duplicate of dird-aneutronic-fusion-propulsion. It is a physically distinct 37-page document with its own DIA document number, DIA-08-1011-004, sequential to DIA-08-1011-003. Cover reads "01 November 2010 / ICOD: 20 July 2010", series "Defense Futures", and uniquely among the eight documents in this batch the byline field is plural, "Authors:", redacted under (b)(6).

Assigned to Teofilo on internal evidence: endnote 17 cites "G. Miley, H. Momota, L. Wu, M. Reilley, V. Teofilo, R. Dell, and R. Hargus, Space Probe Application of IEC Thrusters, Fusion Science and Technology 56 1, 533-539, July 2009", the only occurrence of either candidate author's surname in either aneutronic document. It sits immediately adjacent to endnote 16, a citation of AeroJet/Lockheed Martin Space Systems Company Hall thruster hardware that is also named in the body text. The document's framing is industrial rather than academic: GEO comsat markets, a funding table of privately backed fusion companies, and a closing argument that reactor physicists must now work alongside "the space systems companies".

a.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)

edges.label: deliverable under AAWSAP
edges.note: The released document names the programme itself. Its inside cover reads 'This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency ... Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program' - the redaction between them is (b)(3):10 USC 424. Verified by downloading this DIRD and scanning its full text on 23 August 2026. The scans are OCR-degraded, so the quotation is normalised from the damaged rendering.

edges.label: authored by Lockheed Martin Space Systems staff
edges.note: Follows from the Teofilo attribution. The DIA list gives Teofilo's affiliation of record as Lockheed Martin. Lockheed Martin is the most represented corporate institution on the DIRD author list, with three of the 38 deliverables (Teofilo, Macheret, Golightly).

edges.label: published and holds; DIA-08-1011-004
edges.note: DIA commissioned, holds and released this document. It carries a DIA document number in the DIA-08-xxxx-xxx series on its cover and was released through the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room, whose FileId entry is cited here alongside the retrievable copy. Cover page read on 22 August 2026.

edges.label: series member
edges.note: Membership of the DIRD series is established by the released document itself: its cover page carries the Defense Intelligence Reference Document mark and the DIA Defense Futures banner. Publication date 01 November 2010 on the cover. 37 pages in the released copy. The cover of the scanned release is degraded, so a document number or date is asserted here only where it reads unambiguously.

edges.label: authored (attribution by internal self-citation, see note)
edges.note: TIER 2 AND DELIBERATELY SO. Cover author field is redacted under (b)(6) and reads "Authors" plural, so there may have been co-authors. Assigned to Teofilo because endnote 17 cites "G. Miley, H. Momota, L. Wu, M. Reilley, V. Teofilo, R. Dell, and R. Hargus, Space Probe Application of IEC Thrusters, Fusion Science and Technology 56 1, 533-539, July 2009" - the only occurrence of either candidate author's surname in either aneutronic document - immediately adjacent to a citation of AeroJet/Lockheed Martin Space Systems Hall thruster hardware that also appears in the body text. Paired with the Culbreth edge; if reversed, swap both.

b.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)

edges.label: commissioned subject-matter author
edges.note: Credited with two of the 38 AAWSAP deliverables: 'Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion II' (1 November 2010) and 'Detection and High Resolution Tracking of Vehicles at Hypersonic Velocities' (20 November 2010, DIA-08-1012-001). Both released texts name AAWSAP. Culbreth was based at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, the same city as the prime contractor BAASS. Tier 2: both documents redact their 'Author' field under FOIA exemption (b)(6), so the attribution rests on DIA's separate list of deliverables.

b.label: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS), LLC

edges.label: UNLV academic in the prime contractor's home city
edges.note: TIER 3, INFERENTIAL. AAWSAP was executed by BAASS out of southern Nevada, and BAASS subcontracted subject-matter experts to write the DIRDs. Culbreth was the University of Nevada, Las Vegas faculty member credited with two of them. No document in the public record states that BAASS specifically recruited him, and this edge should not be read as one. Both DIRDs cited here have their author field redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(6), so even the crediting rests on DIA's separate list of deliverables rather than on the documents themselves.
